causalModel.founding: Bog iron forms itself in this ground. A road that eats iron will pay for it.
causalModel.siteAdvantages: A stagnant iron-rich seep where the ore can be lifted from the mud in cakes.
causalModel.occupantsMotive: The diggers come from three villages for one season a year. They consider the work shameful.
causalModel.pressures: The seep is being worked out; each season's cakes are smaller and further from the path.

districts.notes: One mud hut and a furnace floor on the level bench above the seep's north end.

why.what: The bench above the seep: the diggers' hut, the furnace floor and the way down from the road.
why.whyHere: The seep's ore is carried up to the first level ground, where a furnace can stand dry.
why.whySpot: The bench is the last firm ground before the bank drops to the seep.
why.whyNeighbours: The keeper's lodge of the lower Onkobra is 95 m west; the porter yard at Red Cart is 200 m north-west.
why.playerPurpose: A place to take bog iron. The way down leads to the seep where LF67 starts.
why.microGeography: A firm bench, level to within a degree, falling east to a steep bank and the seep.

parcels.orientationWhy: Its door turns east-south-east toward the furnace floor and the way from the road.

why.what: The diggers' hut, a mud pod where the season's crew sleeps.
why.whyHere: The diggers come for one season and need a roof near the furnace.
why.whySpot: The flattest part of the bench, west of the furnace floor and clear of the road.
why.whyNeighbours: The furnace floor is 15 m east; the way from the seep track ends at its door.
why.playerPurpose: A shut room with beds where the crew keeps its stores.
why.microGeography: A mud pod on a levelled pad on the bench.

playerPurpose.note: The season's crew know which end of the seep they stopped working. They also know what took the last digger who went there (LF67).

parcels.orientationWhy: The furnace mouth and its charcoal bed face west-south-west, toward the hut and the path in from the way.

why.what: The furnace floor: Skyrim's smelter (a crafting station, kind pinned prop: its 6.7 m plan is the furnace with its charcoal bed and slag bucket spread round it) with bellows, fuel, ore and an ore cart.
why.whyHere: Ore is smelted where it is dug, so only iron is carried to the road.
why.whySpot: The east end of the bench, at the head of the bank above the seep.
why.whyNeighbours: The diggers' hut is just west; the seep lies below the bank to the east.
why.playerPurpose: Bog iron to take; the furnace is broken open each season to free the bloom.
why.microGeography: A levelled floor of trodden earth on the bench, falling away on the east to the bank over the seep.

interiorClaim.why: 3 of 4 cells plugins link to kotm:argonia/mudhuts/smpodext02 (the base shell of composite:mud/kotm-house-pod) pass; KeebaHouseSnailMinder is a smithy, 1 exterior load door; chosen for this door: A crew's house: three beds, a cook spit and stand at the fire and a huge woodpile, with little personal clutter. KeebaHouseCrafter, the fit rule's first pick, already serves three places (0105 R4 caps a cell at three in the province).

preferCell.why: A crew's house: three beds, a cook spit and stand at the fire and a huge woodpile, with little personal clutter. KeebaHouseCrafter, the fit rule's first pick, already serves three places (0105 R4 caps a cell at three in the province).

routes.why: From the track on the seep's west shore up the bench, past the furnace floor, to the hut door.
From the way across the furnace floor to the furnace mouth.

approaches.sequence: Leaving the track on the seep's west shore, the way climbs north beside the water; the furnace shows first at the top of the rise, then the hut beyond it.
approaches.wayfinding: One way runs north from the track along the shore and up the bench; it passes the furnace floor and ends at the hut door.

networkTerminals.why: The way leaves the track along the seep's west shore and climbs north up the bench to the furnace floor and the hut.

combatSpaces.why: The levelled furnace floor, the one open footing between the hut and the bank.

scaleGrounding.loreSource: catalogue record Bog Iron Workings (works, M1; occupants D2 seasonal diggers, few; interior a dwelling S1, one door)
scaleGrounding.why: A season's crew of three to six from three villages: one sleeping hut with a furnace floor beside it.

candidates.why: A level bench, firm and dry, at the head of the bank above the seep's north end, 25 m south of the road.
The plotted anchor, 60 m south on the seep's west shore.
candidates.rejectedBecause: Ground falling 6-8 degrees with no level cell for a hut pad, 0.23 m over the water table.
